column1: # Site rule (i), legacy named references (Replikanti/interviewscam#64): no
# built HTML or XML file holds '&', one of the 106 names of
# LEGACY_REFERENCES (the WHATWG names that also work without ';') and then
# an ASCII letter, digit or '=' (legacy_reference_problems in
# tools/sitecheck.py). Inside an attribute value HTML keeps such a
# reference as text, while html.parser before Python 3.14 (CI's Ubuntu
# 3.12.3 among them) decodes it there with html.unescape. So
# content="&lt1:x ..." holds the scheme 'lt1:' to the browser and none to
# (o7), and &notx in og:image:alt is the same value as \u{00AC}x in
# twitter:image:alt to (o11) and not to the browser. The rule reads the
# raw text, not a parser's reading, so it refuses such a reference
# anywhere: in a quoted or unquoted value, in an attribute name, an end
# tag, text, a title, a textarea and raw text, where both readings decode
# alike (an over-refusal by design; the minifier writes '&' before
# every ASCII letter, digit and '#'), and also the ';'-names that extend a
# legacy name (∉), which both readings decode. One row per reader of
# the issue, per bound of the follower class and its outer neighbour, per
# name form (an uppercase member, digits in the name, the shortest and the
# longest names), per context, at the start and end of the file, a count
# row, look-alikes that are no such reference in either reading (case,
# truncation, Cyrillic, zero-width and fullwidth characters, the escaped
# and numeric spellings of '&', a follower or a name spelled as a numeric
# reference, ';' then a letter) and the build's own entities, and the two
# XML files Page reads. Attribute rows edit the <h1> into
# <h1 title="a...b">. On a copy of render/pass-intake (the real built
# pages, no built pins) through site_intake_runner in tools/selftest.sh,
# label site-legacyref; the rows with the built pins on are in
# head-cases.tsv. Columns: name, file, find (exactly one occurrence),
# replace, expect (PASS or a text the findings must hold), then further
